concepts.name: MSP: Definition, Legal Status, and Statutory vs. Administrative Nature
key_dimensions: MSP is administratively declared — not backed by a statutory/legal guarantee (key UPSC trap)
Distinction between MSP, Statutory Minimum Price (SMP/FRP for sugarcane), and Market Price
Demand for legal guarantee for MSP and why successive governments have resisted it
Comparison with Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) which has statutory backing under SUGARCANE Act

concepts.name: CACP: Composition, Mandate, and Recommendatory Role
key_dimensions: Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices — statutory vs. non-statutory body (non-statutory, set up in 1965)
CACP recommends MSP but the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approves — CACP has no power to fix
Separate mandates for Kharif, Rabi, and commercial crops
CACP does not recommend MSP for all 23 crops equally — distinction in depth of analysis

concepts.name: Cost Concepts Used in MSP Calculation: A2, A2+FL, and C2
key_dimensions: A2: Actual paid-out costs (seeds, fertilizers, irrigation, hired labour, etc.)
A2+FL: A2 plus imputed value of family labour
C2: Comprehensive cost including imputed rent of owned land and interest on fixed capital — the most contested metric
MS Swaminathan Commission recommendation of C2+50% and government's claim of 1.5x return over A2+FL — the policy trap

concepts.name: Crops Covered Under MSP: The 23-Crop List and its Categorization
key_dimensions: Currently 23 crops: 14 Kharif, 6 Rabi, and 2 commercial crops (sugarcane has FRP, not MSP)
Oilseeds, pulses, coarse cereals inclusion vs. fruits and vegetables exclusion — rationale
Jute and copra are the two commercial crops covered — frequently tested
MSP for paddy and wheat dominates procurement; other 21 crops remain largely aspirational

concepts.name: Price Support Scheme (PSS) vs. MSP: Procurement Mechanism
key_dimensions: PSS is a central scheme under which NAFED/FCI procure oilseeds, pulses, and copra when market prices fall below MSP
FCI handles wheat and rice; NAFED handles oilseeds and pulses — institutional division is a UPSC trap
Losses incurred during PSS procurement are borne by the central government, not states
Difference between MSP declaration and actual procurement — declaration does not ensure farmer receives MSP

concepts.name: FCI's Role in MSP-linked Procurement and Buffer Stock Norms
key_dimensions: Food Corporation of India procures wheat and rice at MSP to build buffer stocks
Buffer stock norms vs. actual stock levels — India frequently exceeds norms (overhang problem)
Decentralized procurement scheme (DCP): states procure on behalf of central government
MSP procurement is concentrated in Punjab, Haryana, and MP — regional skew problem

concepts.name: Market Intervention Scheme (MIS): Scope and Distinction from MSP
key_dimensions: MIS is invoked for perishable commodities (fruits, vegetables, spices) not covered under MSP
Triggered when market prices fall by 10% below cost of production — state must request centre
Cost shared between Centre and States (75:25 for general states; 90:10 for NE/hilly states)
MIS is temporary and crop/season-specific — not a permanent price floor unlike MSP

concepts.name: Price Deficiency Payment (PDP) Model: Bhavantar Bhugtan Yojana as a Case Study
key_dimensions: PDP pays farmers the difference between MSP and actual market price without physical procurement
Madhya Pradesh's Bhavantar Bhugtan Yojana — first large-scale PDP experiment in India
Limitations: farmers sold produce early to avoid price discovery manipulation; trader collusion
Comparison with direct income support (PM-KISAN) vs. price support — fiscal and targeting efficiency debate

concepts.name: Swaminathan Commission Recommendations and MSP Reform Debate
key_dimensions: National Commission on Farmers (2004–06) chaired by M.S. Swaminathan — 5 reports
Key recommendation: MSP = C2 + 50% (comprehensive cost plus 50% profit margin)
Government's counter: already provides 50% return over A2+FL — the definitional dispute
Other Swaminathan recommendations: land reforms, water policy, credit access — holistic vs. MSP-only focus

concepts.name: MSP and WTO Compatibility: Aggregate Measurement of Support (AMS)
key_dimensions: WTO's Agreement on Agriculture (AoA) limits trade-distorting domestic support (Amber Box)
India's MSP + procurement can constitute Amber Box support if it exceeds 10% of value of production (de minimis clause for developing countries)
India's argument: food procurement for public distribution is Green Box (food security purposes)
Peace Clause (Bali 2013): protects developing countries from legal challenge on public stockholding temporarily — India's negotiating position

concepts.name: Factors Considered by CACP Beyond Cost: Demand-Supply, Terms of Trade, and Price Trends
key_dimensions: CACP considers: cost of production, demand-supply balance, domestic and international price trends, inter-crop price parity
Terms of trade between agriculture and non-agriculture sectors (ToT) as a welfare metric
Inflation implications of MSP hike — RBI's concern about MSP as a cost-push inflation driver
CACP's consideration of effect on consumers and the general price level — balance between farmer and consumer interests

concepts.name: MSP for Oilseeds and Pulses: Strategic Importance and Procurement Challenges
key_dimensions: India is import-dependent for edible oils (palm oil) and periodically for pulses — MSP as import substitution tool
NAFED's limited procurement capacity and storage infrastructure as a bottleneck
Pulse MSP often not realized in market — gap between announced MSP and farm-gate price
National Food Security Mission targets for pulses and oilseeds linked to MSP incentive structure

concepts.name: Sugarcane Pricing: FRP vs. SAP and the Dual Price Mechanism
key_dimensions: Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP): statutory, set by CCEA on CACP recommendation, binding on sugar mills
State Advised Price (SAP): set by state governments, typically higher than FRP — legally enforceable in that state
Sugar mills' arrears problem: mills unable to pay even FRP due to financial stress — distinction between legal obligation and capacity
FRP linked to recovery rate of sugar from cane (basic recovery of 10.25%) — incentive structure for efficiency

concepts.name: PM-AASHA Scheme: Three-Component Architecture
key_dimensions: Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay SanraksHan Abhiyan (2018) — umbrella scheme with three pillars
Pillar 1: Price Support Scheme (PSS); Pillar 2: Price Deficiency Payment Scheme (PDPS); Pillar 3: Private Procurement & Stockist Scheme (PPSS) — pilot only
PDPS covers oilseeds only; PSS covers pulses, oilseeds, copra — commodity-wise differentiation is a trap
PPSS: private players procure at MSP and are compensated by government — public-private hybrid model

concepts.name: Decentralized Procurement Scheme (DCP): State vs. Central Procurement
key_dimensions: Under DCP, state governments procure rice/wheat at MSP using their own agencies — FCI provides funds
States retain grain for their own PDS needs; surplus handed to FCI — fiscal flow mechanism
Advantage: reduces FCI's logistical burden; disadvantage: variable state capacity and financial health
States that have adopted DCP vs. those relying on FCI — Chhattisgarh, Odisha as successful DCP examples

concepts.name: Regional Skew in MSP Procurement and Its Consequences
key_dimensions: Over 80% of MSP wheat/rice procurement from Punjab, Haryana, and western UP — geographic concentration
Eastern India (Bihar, UP, WB) farmers rarely benefit due to lack of APMC infrastructure and FCI presence
Consequence: incentivizes water-intensive paddy cultivation in water-scarce Punjab — environmental externality
Reform demand: universalize procurement OR shift to direct income transfer to reduce regional bias

concepts.name: MSP and Crop Diversification: Perverse Incentive Problem
key_dimensions: MSP heavily skewed toward paddy and wheat — creates disincentive to shift to pulses, oilseeds, horticulture
Punjab-Haryana paddy monoculture linked to groundwater depletion — MSP as an indirect ecological driver
NITI Aayog and economic surveys have recommended diversifying MSP basket with assured procurement
Tension: MSP for paddy ensures food security and farmer income but conflicts with sustainable agriculture goals

concepts.name: Electronic National Agriculture Market (e-NAM) and MSP Interaction
key_dimensions: e-NAM: online trading platform linking APMC mandis — aims at price discovery and transparency
If e-NAM prices > MSP, farmers benefit; if below, PSS/PDPS supposed to kick in — design logic
Integration challenges: not all commodities covered, mandi fee structures vary by state, logistics gaps
MSP as a price floor in e-NAM context — whether e-NAM can substitute or complement MSP procurement

concepts.name: Fiscal Cost of MSP Operations and Food Subsidy Accounting
key_dimensions: Food subsidy = difference between economic cost of FCI (procurement + storage + distribution) and central issue price (CIP)
Economic cost includes MSP + mandi charges + transportation + storage — components frequently tested
FCI's mounting debt and borrowing from National Small Savings Fund (NSSF) — off-budget financing of food subsidy
One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) and its link to rationalizing off-take and reducing subsidy leakage

concepts.name: MSP in the Context of Farm Laws 2020 and Their Repeal: Policy Controversy
key_dimensions: Three Farm Laws 2020: Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce Act, Farmers Agreement Act, Essential Commodities Amendment Act
Farmer concern: bypassing APMC mandis would eliminate MSP-linked procurement infrastructure over time
Government position: MSP system was unaffected by the laws — the perception vs. reality gap
Repeal of laws (Nov 2021) and formation of committee on MSP legal guarantee — current policy status and unresolved demand
